AggregateFunction.description: What an [`Expression::Aggregate`] computes over its members.

oneOf.description: How many members there are; takes no `value`.
The sum of the members' values.
The least member value.
The greatest member value.
The members' mean value.
Whether some member's truth `value` holds.
Whether every member's truth `value` holds, and there is a member.
Whether no member's truth `value` holds.
How many distinct values the members have.

The objects a relationship path reaches from the object in scope,
its steps written as a `related` selector's.

The members of the derived group of `grouping` the object in scope
is, or belongs to.

Every object of the project the selector selects, the object in
scope included when it is selected: the counterparts of a pair rule.

The members built-in code measures of the object in scope, by a
list of [`crate::measured::MEASURED_MEMBERS`] written
`name[;key=value…]` (a flight's `steps`). The object in scope stays
the owner; the `value` reads each member's fields in

Citation.description: A reference to one package source.

ColumnKind.description:
The kind of every cell in one table column.

Cells reuse the scalar value variants: a `string` or `textPattern` cell is
a `string` value, a `selector` cell a `selector` value, and so on. A text
pattern is a whole-value wildcard pattern (`*` any run, `?` one character,
`\` escapes the next character).

oneOf.description: A calendar day, written as a `date` value.
An instant with its UTC offset, written as a `dateTime` value.

ComparisonOperator.description:
How a property selector compares the resolved value with its `value`.

`matches` is a regular expression and `like` a wildcard pattern (`*` any
run, `?` one character, `\` escapes); both must match the whole value.
`contains` takes a string, `oneOf` and `noneOf` a string list. The ordered
operators also take a `date` or `dateTime`, compared chronologically.
`exists`, `isEmpty` and `isNotEmpty` judge presence and take no value.

oneOf.description:
Present, but null, blank text or a list of nothing else: the `empty`
presence of `property-requirements`. An absent value is not empty.

Present with a value: the `not-empty` presence of
`property-requirements`. An absent value is not a value.

Date.description: An ISO 8601 calendar date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, optionally with a time zone `Z` or `±hh:mm`.

DateTime.description: An ISO 8601 date-time with an explicit UTC offset, `YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss[.f](Z|±hh:mm)`.

Discipline.description: A discipline name: a lowercase token of at most 64 bytes.

Expression.description:
A node of an expression tree, tagged by `kind` like a [`Selector`].

Every node may carry an author `label` that findings name in place of
the node's rendered form. Operands are evaluated by the engine over
intervals with three-valued truth; `null` is a value the source states
as absent, never a value that could not be read.

[`Selector`]: super::Selector

oneOf.description: A constant of one scalar kind.
The source states no value.

of.description:
Whose property: the object in scope (the default), or, inside an
aggregate's `value` or `where`, the rule's checked object.

oneOf.description: A parameter of the rule, by name.
A derived value the ruleset names.

The `column` cell of the most specific row of the `table` parameter
whose key columns match `keys`, as `keyed-limit` selects a row.

keys.description: The value each key column is matched against, by column ID.

oneOf.description: `antecedent → consequent`.
`left operator right`.

caseSensitive.description: Whether text comparisons respect case; `false` folds both sides.

oneOf.description:
`low ≤ operand ≤ high`, each bound inclusive unless stated
otherwise.
Whether `operand` equals one of `values`.
Whether `operand` equals none of `values`.
Whether `operand` has a value: not `null`.
Whether `operand` is `null`.

The `then` of the first branch whose `when` holds, else `else`. A
ternary is the one-branch case.
The first operand that is not `null`.
Unary minus.
`operand` rounded to the nearest multiple of `step`.
The sine of a plane angle.
The cosine of a plane angle.
The tangent of a plane angle.
The plane angle of the vector `(x, y)`.

A slope restated in another form: `1:12` as a ratio is `8.33` as a
percentage and about `4.76°` as an angle.

An aggregate over the objects `over` reaches from the object in
scope, those `filter` (`where`) selects: `value` is evaluated with
each member in scope. A member whose membership cannot be decided
widens the result or leaves it not evaluated, never dropped.

How the rule `rule` of the same ruleset judged the object in scope:
true when it passed it, false when it reported a finding about it,
`null` when it did not select it, and not evaluated when it left it
open or could not decide whether it selected it. `null` decides no
requirement: guard a reading with [`Expression::Selected`].

Whether the rule `rule` of the same ruleset selected the object in
scope: true or false, and not evaluated when it could not decide.

How many findings the rule `rule` reported about the object in
scope: 0 when it passed or did not select it.

The greatest graded deviation (how far a value misses its bound,
relative to it) of the rule `rule`'s findings about the object in
scope, a plain number; `null` when it reported none graded.
The number of characters of a text.

ExpressionComparison.description:
The binary comparisons of an [`Expression::Compare`].

The ordered operators also take dates and date-times, compared
chronologically. `like` is a wildcard pattern (`*`, `?`, `\` escapes)
and `matches` a regular expression, both over the whole text;
`contains` asks whether the right text occurs in the left.

ExternalName.description:
One external-schema name for a canonical concept.

`type_system` is the release-bound semantic identity the source adapter
declares, for example `https://identifier.buildingsmart.org/uri/buildingsmart/ifc/4`.
Binding a concept to source data requires an exact match on it.

Locator.description: One pinpoint within a cited source.

PackageMetadata.description:
Package identity and presentation metadata.

`name` and `description` are localized in the normalized MCS contract.

columns.description:
The columns of a `table` parameter, in presentation order; empty for
every other kind and then omitted, so existing packages serialize
unchanged.

oneOf.description: An ISO 8601 calendar date.
An ISO 8601 date-time with a UTC offset.
An expression; the capability states the type its value must have.
Rows of typed cells; the definition declares the columns.

An ISO 8601 calendar date, `YYYY-MM-DD`; any other text is refused
when the package is read.

An ISO 8601 date-time with an explicit UTC offset,
`YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss[.f](Z|±hh:mm)`; a date-time without an offset is
refused when the package is read.

An expression the capability evaluates per object
([`Expression`]); type checked when the ruleset is compiled.
Rows of a `table` parameter, in declared order.

Rows of a `table` parameter read from a data file shipped in the
package: a CSV file, or one named sheet of an xlsx workbook.

`path` is relative to the package root, `/`-separated, without `.`
or `..` segments; `sha256` is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the
file's bytes, so the package pins the exact data it was reviewed
with. `columns` declares every column of the file: its header, the
table column it fills and that column's kind. The file is data,
never code: a host loads it before binding
(`axioval_engine::load_table_files`), the binder checks the declared
columns against the parameter's table and binds the rows exactly as
it binds the same rows written inline. A reference that was not
loaded is refused when the package is bound.

sheet.description: The sheet of an xlsx workbook; a CSV file has none.

oneOf.description: The rule's checked object, even inside an aggregate's member scope.
An ISO 8601 calendar date.
An ISO 8601 date-time with a UTC offset.

Quantifier.description:
Which elements of a list value a property selector must hold for.

`all` never holds vacuously: an empty list satisfies neither quantifier,
as an absent value satisfies no comparison.

oneOf.description: At least one element satisfies the comparison.
Every element satisfies it, and there is at least one.

RelatedQuantifier.description: Which of the objects a `related` selector reaches must match its selector.

oneOf.description: At least one reached object matches.
Every reached object matches, and at least one is reached.
No reached object matches; holds when none is reached.

RuleOutcomeKind.description: Which judgement of another rule a `ruleOutcome` selector selects.

oneOf.description: Selected by the rule, and nothing found or left open about it.
The subject of at least one of the rule's findings.

ScalarValue.description:
A literal: one value of a scalar [`ParameterValue`] kind, in the same
wire form. Lists, tables, references and selectors are not literals.

caseSensitive.description: Whether text comparisons respect case; `false` folds both sides.

precision.description:
How finely dates and date-times compare. `day` reads a date-time
as the calendar day it states, so it compares with a date; without
it a date-time compared with a date is not evaluated. Applies to
a `date` or `dateTime` value only.

quantifier.description:
How a list value is compared: `any` element or `all` of them
must satisfy the operator. A scalar value counts as a list of
one. Without it a list value is not evaluated, never compared as
a whole; `exists` takes none.

trim.description: Whether a text value is trimmed of surrounding whitespace first.

oneOf.description:
Objects by the properties whose set and name match XML Schema
patterns, as IDS names them (`Pset_.*Common`).

A pattern matches the whole name the source states; it names no
concept and is never bound through the package vocabulary. Without
`propertySetPattern` every property set is searched. The selector
holds when at least one property matches and the comparison holds
for `matched` of them (`any` or `all`); no matching property is no
match. The other fields compare each matched property's value as a
`property` selector does.

matched.description: Which matched properties must satisfy the comparison.

quantifier.description: How each matched list, bounded or table value is compared.

oneOf.description:
Objects carrying a classification in `system`, as their source
states it.

`code` names one code exactly and `codePattern` matches codes by an
XML Schema pattern over the whole code (`Ss_25_.*`), as IDS writes
classification patterns; at most one of them is given. With neither,
any classification in `system` matches. `includeDescendants` also
matches the codes an assignment's ancestors carry, and needs a code or
a pattern.

Objects a classification of the ruleset (`classifications`)
assigns `class`, or, with `includeDescendants`, `class` or any class
below it in the classification's tree.

An all-match classification selects an object when any class it
assigns does. An unclassified object is not selected; one whose class
cannot be derived is not evaluated. `class` is a declared class of a
hierarchical classification, or a class a flat one's rows assign,
which has no descendants.

The groups a grouping of the ruleset (`groupings`) derives: derived
objects, one per group, never a model object. Only this selector
reaches them, as only an `entityType` reaches resource objects.

Objects by the objects a relationship `path` reaches from them.

Each step is `Relationship` or `Relationship:direction` (`forward`,
the default, `backward` or `either`), walked one after another; a step
ending in `+` is taken one or more times, reaching every object along
the relationship's chain. A step may name several relationships
separated by `|`, with one direction after the last applying to all
(`IfcRelFillsElement|IfcRelVoidsElement:backward+`); it takes any of
them, mixing them along a chain. The reached objects are tested
against `selector` under `quantifier`.

quantifier.description:
Which reached objects must match; `any` is omitted when
serialized.

oneOf.description:
Objects of the sources the host declared to play `value`, such as
`structure`.

A discipline is source metadata, not an object fact: every object of
a source matches or none does. An object whose source declares no
discipline is not evaluated, never a non-match, so a discipline-scoped
rule cannot pass vacuously over a model nobody classified.

Objects of the sources whose metadata `field` satisfies the
comparison, such as the application that wrote a model.

Source metadata is not an object fact: every object of a source
matches or none does. A field compares as a property selector's value
does: one holding several values (a model written by two
applications) needs `quantifier`, and one the source states it lacks
matches nothing, as an absent property does. A source whose field was
never read is not evaluated, never a non-match.

Objects by how another rule of the same ruleset judged them.

`passed` holds for an object the rule `rule` selected and reported
nothing about; `failed` for an object it reported a finding about.
An object the other rule left not evaluated, or could not decide
whether it selected, is not evaluated, never a match or a non-match;
so is every object of a source or project the other rule reported
about as a whole. The plan runs `rule` first; a cycle of such
references fails compilation.

Objects for which `expression`, a truth, holds.

It is evaluated per candidate object with three-valued truth: true
selects, false and `null` do not, and a value that cannot be read
or decided (a measured interval straddling a bound) leaves the object
not evaluated, never skipped. It reads properties, measured and
derived values, never a rule's parameters; it is type checked when
the ruleset is compiled.
Rise over run, a plain number.
Rise over run times 100, a plain number.
The inclination, a plane angle.

Source.description:
A bibliographic source a package may cite. Provenance only: it never changes
selection, evidence, or outcomes.

SourceField.description: A fact about a whole source that a `source` selector compares.

oneOf.description: The file name the host read the source from.
The name of every application the source states wrote it.
The schema the source declares, such as `IFC4`.
The name of the project the source describes.

When the source states it was written, as written: for IFC the
header's `FILE_NAME.time_stamp`.

TableColumnDefinition.description: One named, typed column of a `table` parameter.

required.description: Whether every row must carry a cell in this column.

TableFileColumn.description:
One column of a [`ParameterValue::TableFile`]: the table column `id` it
fills, its `kind` (which must be the parameter column's), the file's
header naming it (`id` when omitted) and, for a `quantity` column, the
unit every cell is stated in.

A `selector` column cannot be read from a file.

TemporalPrecision.description:
How finely a comparison involving a date-time reads it.

Without a precision a date compares with a date and a date-time with a
date-time, as instants. `Day` reads every date-time as the calendar day
it states in its own offset (`2026-09-27T23:30:00-05:00` is on the 27th),
so a date-time can then be compared with a date, or two date-times by
day.

oneOf.description: Compare calendar days only.
